prompt_rules: Show the complete sellable object in the evidence-backed view on pure white. No copy, people, arrows, floating parts, or unpurchased props. Keep all product edges inside the frame.

Make the actual product and assigned proposition clear using the current creative brief. Place exact copy only when assigned, integrated into that composition; related evidence-backed detail regions are allowed. Do not invent accessories.
Show the actual weave/surface orientation at a physically plausible scale. Keep enough product context to identify the surface. No invented layers, fibres, or scientific claims.

Show one evidence-backed assembled or closed connector/clasp state. Preserve component count, interface geometry, strap routing, attachment side and surface orientation. No exploded, lifted, hinged or floating component; no motion arrows.

Show only the evidenced start/end states and verified operating direction. Match contact surfaces and routing in every depicted state. Label arrows only with approved operating copy; never infer a release motion from a static photo.

Depict the assigned recognizable person, meaningful activity and environment with the product readable at natural scale. Choose a pose appropriate to that task; specify visible-limb ownership, contact and occlusion. Preserve plausible anatomy, product curvature and contact shadows without clipping or fused parts.
Present only verified dimensions and compatible variants. Keep measurement lines separate from product contours; avoid illustrating an unsupported device or installation.

For a multi-product selection task, depict each required registered choice as an actual recognizable product with readable differences; swatches or one hero plus colour chips cannot substitute for the range. Swatch cards supply scoped colour/pattern/name evidence, not the output layout or background. Derive the composition from the product and buyer question within the shared background/light/type; keep comparison and scale interpretable without requiring a matrix. Labels use selected final copy only. Explicit swatch-only or single-product closing assignments keep their scope. Preserve identity and texture per SKU; invent no colours or accessories.
